marc:datafield.marc:subfield: 村上T : 我愛的那些 T 恤 | Cunshang T : wo ai de na xie T xu

The T-shirt, originally seen as an undergarment unfit for formal occasions, only rose to fashion prominence after World War II, thanks to screen icons like James Dean and Marlon Brando—rebellious and cool figures of their time. What was once a soldier’s undershirt transformed into stylish casual wear. Today, the T-shirt is more than just clothing—it represents a way of life. In an interview, Haruki Murakami once said, “To me, T-shirts symbolize freedom.” After all, for someone who mostly wears shorts and white sneakers—except when he has to wear a suit (as he mentioned in Murakami Radio 2)—it’s no surprise that the T-shirt fits best with his laid-back lifestyle as a writer.
